title: Inventory Valuation & Errors
description: Learn valuation adjustments and how inventory errors affect financial statements.
html:
Inventory is not always kept at its original cost

Sometimes inventory loses value because of damage, obsolescence, declining selling prices or other economic changes.

Accounting rules may therefore require inventory to be written down.

Lower of Cost and Net Realizable Value

For inventory measured using certain methods, a common valuation approach compares cost with net realizable value (NRV).

NRV = Estimated Selling Price − Costs of Completion, Disposal and Transportation

Example

Assume inventory has:

Recorded Cost $50,000
Net Realizable Value $46,000

If the applicable accounting rule requires the lower amount, inventory would be reported at:

$46,000

The decline is:

$50,000 − $46,000 = $4,000

Inventory errors

Inventory errors are especially important because ending inventory affects both the balance sheet and Cost of Goods Sold.

Beginning Inventory + Purchases − Ending Inventory = COGS

What if ending inventory is overstated?

Suppose actual ending inventory is $20,000, but the company incorrectly reports $25,000.

Ending inventory is overstated by $5,000.

Current-period effects

  • Ending Inventory → Overstated
  • Cost of Goods Sold → Understated
  • Gross Profit → Overstated
  • Net Income → Overstated

Why does COGS become understated?

Look at the formula:

COGS = Beginning Inventory + Purchases − Ending Inventory

If you subtract an ending inventory amount that is too large, calculated COGS becomes too small.

What if ending inventory is understated?

  • Ending Inventory → Understated
  • Cost of Goods Sold → Overstated
  • Gross Profit → Understated
  • Net Income → Understated

CPA thinking

Don't just memorize the arrows.

Start with the COGS formula and determine what happens when ending inventory changes.

quiz.prompt: If ending inventory is overstated, what happens to current-period Cost of Goods Sold?
quiz.explanation: Because ending inventory is subtracted when calculating COGS, overstating ending inventory causes COGS to be understated.

objectives: Explain inventory valuation & errors and its underlying principles.
Apply the topic to a financial-reporting scenario.
Evaluate common errors and their financial-statement effects.
